lessons.title: Check maize for armyworm: the W walk
lessons.summary: A 10-minute field check that tells you whether to act.

steps.text: Walk your field in the shape of a W.
Stop at 5 spots along the W.
At each spot, look closely at 4 plants — 20 plants in all.
Count plants with fresh holes or droppings in the funnel.
0–3 damaged plants: no spray, check again in 3 days. 4 or more: act today.

lessons.title: Making compost
lessons.summary: Turn crop leftovers and manure into free fertilizer.

steps.text: Dig a pit in the shade, about 1 metre wide and deep.
Layer dry material, then green leaves and weeds.
Add manure and a little ash.
Keep it damp, not wet.
Turn it every 2 weeks. It’s ready in about 3 months — dark and crumbly.

lessons.title: Mulching beans before a dry spell
lessons.summary: Keep water in the soil when rain stops.

steps.text: Collect dry grass or crop leftovers.
Spread a thin layer between the rows, not touching stems.
Mulch after rain, while the soil is still moist.

lessons.title: Top-dressing maize at knee height
lessons.summary: The right time and way to add urea.

steps.text: Wait until maize is knee-high and the soil is moist.
Put a small pinch of urea in a ring a hand-width from each plant.
Cover it with soil — uncovered urea escapes into the air.
Don’t apply just before heavy rain.

lessons.title: Storing maize safely
lessons.summary: Dry, clean and airtight storage keeps grain safe to eat.

steps.text: Dry cobs on a tarpaulin, off the ground.
It’s dry when a grain cracks as you bite it.
Store in airtight (hermetic) bags.
Keep bags on pallets, off the floor and walls.
Mark healthy plants before harvest.
Skip any plant with mosaic, brown spots or dry shoots.
Cut pieces about 25 cm long with 5–7 buds.

lessons.title: Spraying safely
lessons.summary: Protect yourself, your family and your water.

steps.text: Use only products on RAB’s approved list, from a registered agro-dealer.
Wear gloves, a mask and long sleeves.
Spray in the calm early morning, never before rain.
Wash hands and clothes after spraying; keep children away.
Never reuse empty containers for water or food.
Guide roof water into a tank or drum with a gutter.
Dig a lined pit at the bottom of the field.
Use stored water for seedlings during dry spells.
